## Agreement with the HRS/HCAP Algorithm

```{r}
analysis2_agreement |>
  dplyr::filter(
    classification_2 == "HRS/HCAP Algorithm",
    classification_1 %in% c("Core Algorithm", "PMM")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    classification_1 = dplyr::recode(classification_1, "Core Algorithm" = "Core algorithm"),
    n = c(
      "Core algorithm" = analysis2_n_compare[["core_algorithm"]],
      "PMM" = analysis2_n_compare[["pmm"]]
    )[classification_1]
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(classification_1, n, three_class_kappa, binary_kappa) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "classification_1") |>
  gt::tab_stubhead("Compared with HRS/HCAP Algorithm") |>
  gt::cols_label(
    n = "N",
    three_class_kappa = "Normal, MCI, Dementia (weighted kappa)",
    binary_kappa = "Dementia vs. no dementia (kappa)"
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = n) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(three_class_kappa, binary_kappa), decimals = 2) |>
  gt::opt_stylize(6, color = "gray") |>
  gt::tab_options(
    table.width = gt::pct(90),
    table.font.size = gt::px(26),
    column_labels.font.size = gt::px(22),
    stub.font.size = gt::px(24),
    data_row.padding = gt::px(6)
  )
```

<div style="font-size: 0.5em; line-height: 1.2;">
HRS/HCAP 2016 participants. Kappa measures agreement beyond chance (0 = chance, 1 = perfect). The three-class kappa uses quadratic weights, so a Normal vs. MCI disagreement counts less than a Normal vs. Dementia disagreement. All kappas use HCAP population weights (HCAP16WGTR). Both the Core algorithm and the PMM are calibrated and scored in the same sample, so its agreement is an in-sample estimate.
</div>
